architecture.deployment: Local proxy: each MCP client launches its servers through `sievant proxy` (sievant wrap)
architecture.identity: static: the stdio process is the agent
agents: one local agent per wrapped server
stages: Policy: is this agent allowed this tool, prompt or resource, with these arguments
Input checks: credentials and personal data in the arguments
Forward to the MCP server (SSRF guard, response size cap)
Output checks: redaction, prompt-injection scoring, row and byte budgets

controls.name: Enforcement mode (enforce or observe)
controls.detail: Mode enforce: policy decisions stop the calls they refuse.

controls.name: Agent authentication and identity
controls.detail: Each wrapped server is reached only by the client process that launched it (stdio); its calls are recorded under the agent name the wrap gives.

controls.name: Transport security for agent connections
controls.detail: stdio: agents reach Sievant through a local pipe, not the network.

controls.name: MCP client servers routed through Sievant
controls.detail: Client configurations were not read for this report.

controls.name: Deny-by-default policies for tools, prompts and resources, per agent
controls.detail: Deny by default, but `sievant proxy` allows every tool of the server it fronts; per-agent allowlists need a configuration file.

controls.name: Schema validation and argument constraints (min, max, in, matches, path_under, url_hosts)
controls.detail: No argument constraints; arguments are still validated against each tool's input schema.

controls.name: Path and URL argument rules for every tool
controls.detail: No path or URL argument rules (packs fs-paths and egress).

controls.name: Credentials and personal data in tool arguments blocked or redacted
controls.detail: Credentials in arguments: block; personal data in arguments: audit.

controls.name: Credentials and personal data redacted from tool results
controls.detail: Results are redacted before the agent sees them: email, credit_card, us_ssn, jwt, aws_access_key, pem_private_key, password.

controls.name: Prompt-injection detection on arguments and results (flag, annotate, block)
controls.detail: Arguments and results are scored and suspect ones recorded (action flag); nothing is blocked or annotated.

controls.name: Tool definitions read once, pinned, and pinned on first use
controls.detail: No wrapped servers were found.

controls.name: Upstream resources and prompts not served unchecked
controls.detail: Upstream resources and prompts are withheld unless a connector serves them, and served ones pass the output checks.

controls.name: Rate limits per agent and per tool
controls.detail: Rate limits: 50 calls a second per agent by default (bursts of 100).

controls.name: Row, byte and response-memory budgets
controls.detail: Results are capped at 65536 bytes and 1000 rows; row and byte budgets limit what an agent reads over time.

controls.name: SSRF guard on outbound connectors
controls.detail: No network connectors.

controls.name: Client configuration audit (sievant scan)
controls.detail: Client configurations were not read for this report.

controls.name: Audit trail of every call and security event
controls.detail: Every call and security event is recorded in the local audit store, kept 30 days; inputs are sanitized and keyed with an HMAC, so a record can be matched to its input without storing it.

gaps.title: No audit trail to report on
gaps.detail: The audit store could not be read (no audit database there yet), so this report shows configuration only, no activity.
gaps.fix: Run Sievant (sievant proxy through sievant wrap, or sievant serve) so it records calls, and point --audit at its store.

gaps.title: Wrapped servers allow every tool
gaps.detail: `sievant proxy` checks every call but allows every tool of the server it fronts, so no per-agent allowlist limits what an agent can call.
gaps.fix: Write a configuration (sievant init --profile balanced or strict), let it observe, then narrow it with sievant policy suggest and apply.

gaps.title: Suspected prompt injection is recorded, not acted on
gaps.detail: With action flag, suspect results reach the model unchanged; the audit trail records them.
gaps.fix: Set injection.action to annotate (the injection pack) or block for the agents that need it.

gaps.title: Personal data in tool arguments is passed on
gaps.detail: sanitization.input_pii is audit: personal data the agent puts into arguments reaches the backend; the audit record notes it, sanitized.
gaps.fix: Set sanitization.input_pii to redact or block (pack secrets-pii).

gaps.title: MCP client configurations were not checked
gaps.detail: This report did not read the MCP client configurations, so it cannot say which servers bypass Sievant.
gaps.fix: Run sievant report without --no-clients, or sievant scan.
